title: 'Yesterday' was 'Scrambled Eggs'
hook: Paul McCartney woke up with the tune of Yesterday and sang about eggs.
peek: One of the most recorded songs ever arrived in a dream. Paul McCartney woke with the melody of Yesterday complete, and for months he sang it with stand-in words: Scrambled eggs, oh my baby how I love your legs.
lede: In the mid-1960s, Paul McCartney woke one morning in London with a full melody in his head. He went straight to a piano to catch it before it faded. The tune felt so finished that he was sure he must have heard it somewhere. Without real lyrics yet, he sang placeholder lines to keep it in his memory, starting with Scrambled eggs.

bullets.text: McCartney played the tune to friends and music people for weeks, asking whether they recognised it. Only when nobody did was he convinced that the melody was his own.
The working lyric ran Scrambled eggs, oh my baby how I love your legs. McCartney has happily sung it in interviews, and it fits the melody's rhythm almost exactly.

bullets.opening: Lyrics on a Portugal road trip
bullets.text: The real words came in 1965, reportedly on a long car journey in Portugal. The silly breakfast line became Yesterday, all my troubles seemed so far away.
On the 1965 recording, McCartney sings with his acoustic guitar and a string quartet, and no other Beatle plays. It went on to become one of the most covered songs in history.
